status: development protocol fixed before scoring; not pristine confirmation
hypothesis: At matched baryonic Newtonian acceleration, lower stellar surface density predicts greater observed acceleration.
scope: Existing 139-galaxy exploration photometry only; reserved confirmation sample excluded.
primary_feature: log10(0.5 SBdisk + 0.7 SBbul), stellar surface mass density proxy, not total or 3D density
selection: Q<=2; 30<=inclination<=80 degrees; positive radius, speed, baryonic inward force and stellar surface density; published velocity error/speed <=0.1; at least five retained positions per galaxy
mass_model: Vbar^2 = Vgas abs(Vgas) + 0.5 Vdisk^2 + 0.7 Vbul^2; missing molecular gas is a limitation
prediction: Leave one entire galaxy out. Equal total training weight per galaxy. Compare fitted one-scale RAR and fixed-knot flexible acceleration-only baseline with the same baselines plus one linear concentration residual. Feature residualization uses training data only.
support: At least five other galaxies within 0.15 dex in predicted acceleration and target concentration within the range of those training positions. Identical scoring support for all models.
matched_pairs: Per-galaxy medians in fixed 0.1-dex acceleration bins; cross-galaxy acceleration difference <=0.05 dex and stellar concentration difference >=0.5 dex. Greedy closest acceleration match, largest concentration contrast as tie breaker; each galaxy occurs in at most one pair. Published fixed RAR removes small acceleration mismatch for this descriptive test only.
sensitivities: disk M/L 0.4 and 0.6; bulge 1.4 times disk
controls: Target mutation cannot alter match selection
Held-out target mutation cannot alter its predictions
Synthetic acceleration-only null and injected negative concentration effect
Shared stellar mass error null simulations, 64 draws with 0.1 dex galaxy-wide mass-to-light errors; not a full uncertainty posterior
uncertainty: Galaxy bootstrap of cross-validation score differences and pair bootstrap for disjoint pairs; descriptive development stability intervals, not discovery significance. Do not count radii as independent galaxies.
decision: A promising pattern must have the expected negative coefficient, improve whole-galaxy prediction beyond both baselines and survive sensitivity checks. A stellar proxy result cannot confirm total-volume-density coherence.
